notes: FIVE CONTENT BANDS, FOUR OF THEM BLOCKS. In DOM order the page is #first-visit,
#services, #reviews, #faq, #membership. The first four are the block list below; the
fifth stays a TEMPLATE band and is exempted under `sections`, with its reason there.
WHY LEAVING #membership BEHIND IS ORDER-SAFE. An unguarded band renders where it sits in
the .astro file, which is after the whole block run — so bands left behind only keep page
order while they are a contiguous TAIL. #membership is band 5 of 5, so it is. Migrating a
sixth band after it later, or adding a block below it, is the LocalTrust fault that put
the practice band at the bottom of /cosmetic-dentistry/clear-aligners/. Recorded as a
known gap on this route so the next person meets it before they cause it.
NO RAIL ON THIS ROUTE. /new-patients/ has no `.toc` nav and pageFields.tocLinks is null on
the live endpoint (checked, not assumed), so `nav_label` resolves blank on all four blocks
— the map's own default — and the template carries no derivedTocLinks loop. Nothing to
lose and nothing to keep in step. The template says so in as many words rather than
carrying a loop that feeds nothing.
BAND VOCABULARY, READ OFF THIS SHEET AND NOT OFF THE CLASS NAMES. `.section.alt` is the
DARK one here (new-patients.css:81 -> --vs-charcoal-green, colour #fff) and `.section.dark`
is the PALE one (new-patients.css:84 -> --vs-sage-pale, colour --vs-ink). A bare
`.section` gets padding only (new-patients.css:80) so the body paper shows through. Every
`band` below is resolved from those three rules.
THE PAGE SHEET LOSES EVERY (0,2,0) TIE WITH A BLOCK, AND THAT IS MEASURED. Astro 6.1.9
compiles ATTRIBUTE scoping, so a block's `.process-card` is `.process-card[data-astro-cid-…]`
at (0,2,0) — the same weight as this sheet's `.np .process-card`. The tie is settled by
bundle order, and the built pages put PageBlocks' bundle LAST: dist/general-dentistry/index.html
links _assets/_astro_content.css, then the page's own index_astro.css, then BaseLayout.css,
then PageBlocks.Dx0ulujF.css. So on every migrated band the BLOCK's declarations win and
this sheet's `.np` rules for that band go inert. Three consequences are itemised in the
`known_gaps` below; the rest (`.wrap` padding, the `.section-head` hairline eyebrow, the
centred 760px head) are the same across all fifteen already-migrated routes and are the
shape of this phase, not a fault of this page.
ONE CLASS TOKEN IS LOST AND IT IS INERT. #first-visit, #reviews and #faq write
`<div class="section-head center">` (index.astro:236, :293, :312); no block emits the
`center` token. It is inert because the block's own `.section-head` is already
`max-width: 760px; margin: 0 auto 64px; text-align: center` (ProcessStepsBlock.astro:507-511,
FaqBlock.astro:300-304) and wins the tie above — the same centring `.np .section-head.center`
(new-patients.css:92-95) applies today.

num_is_moved_not_derived: `num` comes from the card's `meta`, which holds "01" through "06" — verified against the
live endpoint, all six rows. @index2 is the derivation the pilot uses only because the

row beats deriving a value whenever both exist. @index2 would not work here in any case:
vs_bb_resolve_rows() reads it in the process_steps/faqs branch and never in the `cards`
why_the_zip: The 6 firstVisit rows are in the CMS and carry meta, title and body — but not the
`.step-tag` label, because the legacy `cards` repeater is group/title/body/meta/href and
has no `tag`. Verified live: all six rows come back with href null and no tag anywhere.
So the six tags are transcribed from the `firstVisit` array at
new-patients/index.astro:107-138 and zipped on in template order. Dropping them would
strip "Step One" through "Step Six" off the six cards, which is the sequence the band is
about. The zip refuses on a length mismatch (backfill-blocks.php:457-469), so six literal
rows against six card rows is checked, not trusted.

known_gaps: THE ONE-COLUMN BREAKPOINT MOVES FROM 479 TO 780, and no field can hold it back.

new-patients.css:347 takes it to one column at 479px. ProcessStepsBlock collapses to two
at 991 (:1199-1209) — the same step — but to ONE at 780 (:1219-1232). Between 480px and

are (0,3,0) compounds inside media queries and the block's bundle loads last, so the

Closed either by giving process_steps its own collapse field (the service_cards precedent,
vs-content-model.php:4205-4230) or by adding a 479 step to ProcessStepsBlock's own rules.
Recorded rather than fixed: neither file is this route's to edit, and the sheet is not
this migration's to edit either.

vs-content-model.php:4141 and it changes no fragment character, so neither query
validation nor scripts/check-block-schema.mjs can see it — the same blind spot the
manifest records for `process_steps`' fifth column. ServiceCardsBlock.astro has no
branch for it: :601-620 is one shape, and `isFeatures` is the only fork. A row saved
with this value therefore renders the `tiles` shape — the <h3> moves DOWN into

page has never drawn. That is four cards restructured on a live band.
Closed by the branch the Wave-B contract specifies: same `a.svc-card.compact` and
`.svc-img`, `.svc-body` = <h3> -> p.svc-desc -> an EMPTY `.svc-row-bot` holding a bare
<span>, no badge. The empty span is vestigial and is reproduced anyway — the phase is
graded on the built HTML and dropping it is a diff nobody asked for.
2. `collapse_at: "479"` IS REGISTERED IN PHP AND NOT READ BY THE COMPONENT.
ServiceCardsBlock.astro:356 is `String(collapseAt ?? "").trim() === "780" ? "780" : "640"`
— a two-value test, so "479" falls through to "640". Two measurable losses follow:
* the grid collapses to one column at 640px where this page collapses at 479
(new-patients.css:348), so between 480 and 640 the four tiles read one across
instead of two; and the block's 1100px two-column step (:1283-1289) fires where
this page's is 991 (new-patients.css:339), so between 992 and 1100 they read two
across instead of four.
* the <Image> `sizes` hint becomes the `tiles-4` string
"(max-width: 640px) 100vw, (max-width: 1100px) 50vw, 25vw" where the template ships
"(max-width: 479px) 100vw, (max-width: 991px) 50vw, 25vw" (index.astro:272). Wrong
`sizes` is not a layout bug — the browser picks a different candidate — but it is
still a change to a live page.
Closed by the third branch plus an IMAGE_SPEC entry, both named in the Wave-B contract.
